subtopic: Hash Maps, Heaps and Disjoint-Set Unions (DSU)
question_text: In Robin Hood Hashing, what displacement metric is used to determine whether an incoming key evicts an existing occupant during linear probing?

options.text: Probe Sequence Length (distance of occupant from its initial hashed bucket)

answer_explanation: Robin Hood hashing steals from the 'rich' (keys close to their home bucket, having small probe sequence lengths) and gives to the 'poor' (keys displaced far from their home bucket), reducing the variance of lookup probe lengths.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: Robin Hood hashing steals from the 'rich' (keys close to their home bucket, having small probe sequence lengths) and gives to the 'poor' (keys displaced far from their home bucket), reducing the variance of lookup probe lengths.
